note: Agents MUST load human-sounding-writing (hsw) before writing GitHub prose (PR and issue titles and bodies, issue-log titles, comments, commits, receipts, changelog prose) and human-output-naming (hon) before naming files the stack itself writes. This router does not decide how a project's own README, product pages, marketing or sales sites, demo pages or HTML are written: those follow the owner's direction, and writing-direction is loaded there only when the owner asks (agent-stack-train#117). The sales-arc route marketing_intro_site is retired. HTML pages need no writing module (agent-stack-train#81). Soft = no NLP CI grade of prose; presence of modules + this contract (including the always-on inject) is what validate_content_system and verify_hsw_applied check. EVERY CGM adopter must inject the always-on system_block into agent prompts at start (see acs_prompt_inject / always_on_system_block).

routes.notes: Opt-in only (agent-stack-train#117): the owner's direction decides how a README or product page is written. Load writing-direction here only when the owner asks for it. Never required.

Reader-facing product/research explanations (plans, architecture writeups, evidence briefs) route to writing-direction: story order, scan-first selective bold, evidence/status/boundaries distinct, clear next action. This is NOT manuscript/data-writeup prose — a scholarly paper or raw data writeup routes to human-sounding-writing (hsw) instead. Do not copy the README outline mechanically onto a brief; adapt the checks to the document type.
review_checklist: Story order: name the recognizable human situation, then the concrete problem and consequence, before mechanism or architecture.
Connect each important paragraph to why it matters and to an evidence, example, or boundary — not to style alone.
Keep evidence, status, and boundaries distinct: say what a cited source supports, what it leaves unproven, and the inspected revision.
Use descriptive headings and selective bold so a heading-and-bold scan tells a usable second story; do not turn the brief into a README clone.
End with a clear next action, example, or smallest useful path for the reader.
Adapt the checks to the document type; do not add promotional claims a research brief does not support.

routes.notes: Human voice, AI-tell scrub, restrained bold. Includes chart/takeaway guidance for papers and data writeups. Commit messages and commit subjects are in scope — MUST load hsw before writing them. HTML pages (reports, compare HTML/UIs, appendable HTML, other agent-produced HTML) are not in scope since agent-stack-train#81; see not_routed. Filename basenames stay on human-output-naming (hon). Receipts (push, checkpoint, release) are human-facing prose and route here too; the title and reference rules are in docs/NARRATIVE_AUTHORITY.md.

title_contract.rule: A title is one complete, understandable human sentence stating what is wrong or what the reader gets. No leading prefix codes (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:, refactor:, test:, ci:, build:, perf:, style:, revert:) and no internal task numbers (#45, CGM-0045, TASK-0045, M5) as the first token.
title_contract.reference_rule: Give every commit SHA, pull request number, flag, or file path a plain-English meaning in the same sentence before it carries weight.
checklist: Read the title alone: does it state what is wrong or what the reader gets?
Strip any leading prefix code or internal task number; the title must still read as one human sentence.
Name what each SHA, pull request number, flag, or file path is before it does any work.
No colon-reveal slogan; the title is a sentence, not a label with a subtitle.

routes.notes: Filesystem names for generated media and manifest paths. Default speakable basenames (identity first; omit defaults); optional style=safe_twin. Reject hashy junk and robot key=value stems. Keep a per-feature filename legend (glossary + file list). See docs/HUMAN_OUTPUT_NAMING.md.

not_routed.reason: Retired for HTML on 2026-11-01 (agent-stack-train#81): no writing module is required before writing an HTML page. Marketing intro sites, sales sites and technical demo pages are not routed either (agent-stack-train#117): the owner decides how they read.

Not routed (agent-stack-train#117): CGM helps with GitHub prose, not with how a project writes its own product. The route marketing_intro_site and the required README load are retired; load writing-direction only when the owner asks.

apply_checklist: Identify the writing surface. If it is GitHub prose (PR title/body, issue title/body, issue-log title, comment, commit message/subject, receipt, changelog prose), MUST load modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md before drafting; do not skip because it is short or 'just a commit'.
Apply the module rules to the draft (voice, AI-tell scrub, bold policy as the module states).

A README, product page, marketing or sales site, demo page or HTML page is NOT governed by CGM: follow the owner's direction. Load writing-direction only when the owner asks for it (agent-stack-train#117).

Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs route to writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations); apply its review_checklist. A scholarly paper or raw data writeup still routes to hsw.

If the surface is a filename the stack itself writes (generated artifact, asset-manifest path, committed media basename, filename legend), MUST load modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md (hon), call scripts/human_filename (speakable by default; optional safe_twin), and keep a per-feature legend.
Never treat HSW as optional or per-task opt-in for GitHub prose.

acs_prompt_inject.when: At agent start / session boot for EVERY repo that pins CGM — not per-task and not ACS-only. Paste system_block into the agent system prompt before the agent writes GitHub prose (PRs, issues, issue logs, comments, commits, receipts) — and before naming files the stack itself writes.
acs_prompt_inject.system_block:
CGM ALWAYS-ON WRITING RULE (every adopter that pins this helper)

Before you write GitHub prose — PR and issue titles and bodies, issue-log titles, comments, commit messages, receipts, changelog prose — you MUST load and apply modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md (hsw).

This rule is always on for that prose. Opt-in is forbidden. Do not wait for a per-task flag.

This rule does not cover the project's own product. READMEs, product pages, marketing or sales sites, demo pages and HTML pages follow the owner's direction; no writing module is required, and writing-direction is loaded only when the owner asks. HTML pages need no writing module.

Exceptions (only these):
- Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs → load modules/writing-direction/SKILL.md (reader-facing explanation, not a manuscript or data writeup)
- Filenames the stack itself writes (generated artifacts, asset-manifest paths, media basenames, filename legends) → load modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md (hon)

If you cannot load a required skill file from the pinned CGM checkout, stop and report that.

Filenames the stack writes: use scripts/human_filename (speakable basenames; optional safe_twin) and keep a per-feature legend. Hash may stay a separate manifest field.
acs_prompt_inject.instruction: ALWAYS-ON for every CGM adopter (ACS is one consumer, not the only one). Paste acs_prompt_inject.system_block into the agent system prompt at start. HSW (human-sounding-writing) is ON by default for GitHub prose. Before writing it, MUST load modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md. Opt-in is forbidden; always_on is true; HSW is not optional for GitHub prose. HTML pages need no writing module. Pull request titles/bodies, issue titles/bodies, issue-log titles, comments, commit messages, receipts and changelog prose → human-sounding-writing (hsw). README, product pages, marketing and sales sites, demo pages and HTML pages are not routed (agent-stack-train#117, #81): follow the owner's direction. Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs → writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations). Soft enforcement means no NLP CI grade of prose; the contract language is MUST/APPLY/default_on/always_on. Follow apply_checklist and human_facing_default in this file. Filenames the stack itself writes → human-output-naming (hon): MUST load that skill and use scripts/human_filename with speakable basenames; keep a per-feature legend; never opaque p0/hex stems.

human_facing_default.notes: Default ON for GitHub prose. Do not treat HSW as optional or per-task. README, product pages, marketing and sales sites, demo pages and HTML are not routed (agent-stack-train#117, #81): the owner decides. Reader-facing research plans, architecture explanations and evidence briefs stay on writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations route); filenames the stack itself writes stay on human-output-naming (hon).

always_on_system_block.notes: Canonical paste text lives at acs_prompt_inject.system_block (name kept for pin compatibility). Every CGM adopter must inject it at agent start.

bootstrap_steps: At session start, read .content-system/ and the pinned CGM checkout; do not read the helper's moving main.
Paste acs_prompt_inject.system_block into the agent system prompt before writing GitHub prose; opt-in is forbidden.

MUST load modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md for PR/issue/commit prose, and modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md for filenames the stack writes. README and product pages follow the owner's direction.
Generate the full narrative image set (hero PNG raster, problem, supporting) and register each in .content-system/asset-manifest.json with a prompt record; never use an SVG as the README hero.
Before handoff, run validate_content_system.py --check-adopter-readme (or verify_adopter_content.py) and fix failures.
antigravity.notes: Google Antigravity reads .content-system but did not proactively load the deep writing guidance (issue #35). This entry points the agent at the always-on system block and the full-depth README requirements. See docs/ANTIGRAVITY_INTEGRATION.md.
